utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before I invite Madam Registrar [sic] to escort the witness into the courtroom for which, by the way, I think the curtains have to be pulled down, I would first give the reasons for the protective measures the Chamber granted in respect of Witness 3. On the 31st of August 2007, the Prosecution applied for the trial-related protective measures of pseudonym and face and voice distortion for Witness 3. The Chamber has been informed that the Defence does not oppose the motion. The Chamber has set out the standard for granting protective measures in numerous decisions and therefore sees no need to repeat them again. The witness has expressed fear for his safety and that of his family should it become publicly known that he gave evidence for the Prosecution. The Chamber notes that close family members of Witness 3 live in Kosovo. Given the nature of the witness's anticipated testimony, the Chamber is satisfied that it may antagonise persons who reside in their community. The Chamber finds that the requirements for granting protective measures have been met and therefore grants the Prosecution's motion. And this concludes the Chamber's reasons for the decision on protective measures for Witness 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness 3. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 3, I'd like to remind you that the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony still binds you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see on my screen that we returned into open session. Mr. Registrar, if that is confirmed, yes, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just before Mr. Di Fazio addresses you, I'm not sure what the issue is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understood that there was an issue about apart from the core of the testimony of the witness, that there would be some reputation evidence or something like that to be elicited from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May we discuss this? Because no notice has been given to me of what it is that may be an issue between this witness and any other party. Perhaps we could use the break to discuss Mr. Di Fazio's concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if Mr. Di Fazio uses one or two lines to explain to us what the issue is, and then we will give an opportunity to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It doesn't concern anyone except --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It concerns my clients, it's very clear, Mr. Di Fazio indicated that he intends to lead reputation evidence with regard to my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what type do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's in paragraphs 50, 51, 52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll have a look at that. That's what you want to elicit from this witness. Let me just check whether I --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I don't know if you wish to -- for me to at least to begin to address this because that needs to be considered in light of the fact that as Mr. Di Fazio knows, that when the witness number 3 was shown a photo spread and asked whether or not he could identify any individual in photo lineup number 4, which my client was in photograph position number 6, the witness said, and I quote, "I don't know any one of the persons shown on the lineup."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So we start with that being the context in which Mr. Di Fazio intends on introducing reputation evidence with regard to my client, of which I have a fair amount to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. They read it. The reference to the paragraphs are references to the 2007 statement, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's right, the recent statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The recent statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the reference that I made is paragraph number 73 which is ERN number U 0086978 and the photo line up was shown at U 0086985. That was shown to Mr. Haverinen back in 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I haven't led any evidence of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again could I press for sometime to consider this over the adjournment because those paragraphs contain all sorts of information which, when looked at in conjunction with other paragraphs, proves to have been put in a rather different framework from the which in which the witness is able to support it, and it cuts across material beyond the reputation of Mr. Balaj. So perhaps we might just have a sensible opportunity to discuss what it is Mr. Di Fazio is proposing to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This Chamber -- reputation evidence is not the kind of evidence that assists the Chamber most, to say it politely. We will consider during the break looking at these paragraphs, keeping in mind of what you said, whether we will grant any additional time for Mr. Di Fazio to elicit this evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour totally separate matter since I think we are finished with that one for the moment. May I very respectfully draw your attention to your own words at line -- page 68, line 24 when you put to the witness your understandable surprise, perhaps, that he seems to keep rushing back to Jabllanice despite all the perils that allegedly await him there, you put this to him: "You escaped from Jabllanice prison." I do know that the Bench, the Tribunal, fully understands that it is not accepted on behalf of any of the defendants that there ever was a prison at Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do agree with you from -- he said he was arrested and at least he explained -- I'll not use that word again. To what extent the place where someone is detained and ill treated, whether you would call that a prison or detention place, or deaths are caused, you pay specific attention to the word "prison." I appreciate that you do it and why you do it, and when I used this word, this was not in anticipation of any finding on the presence of a prison, and I will of course, if I would put that question again to the same witness, I would use a different phrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I felt confident that was the case, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn until five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, before we -- would you like to address the repetition evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. If -- unless the Trial Chamber has reached a provisional view in favour of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have reached a provisional view in favour of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In that case I will address you if I need to, if Mr. Di Fazio seeks to persuade you to take the contrary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is, that the evidence which the Chamber could expect that would be elicited in relation to the witness statement, paragraph 50, 51, and 52, that the Chamber has read it, has seen that it's mainly unsubstantiated hearsay evidence, not to say that there are a few facts here and there, but in order to elicit this in a way which would be acceptable for the Chamber would take quite some time. And also in view of the non-contradicted observations by Mr. Guy-Smith, as far as photo spreads and the appearance of the accused on this photo spread and the witness not recognising any of these persons, the Chamber in view of all this would expect that it takes so much time that it's not granting that additional time to the Defence. So the Chamber is not saying that under no circumstances what is said here, which is hearsay, that it's impossible to substantiate it, but for the very practical reasons, also in view of the time schedule of the witness, also in view of the estimate given by the Prosecution, how much time they would need, taken all together, the Chamber does not grant any additional time to the Prosecution to elicit such evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if I could just make a request for two minutes before the end of today's session just to address briefly the question of the outstanding motion in connection with an additional videolink, at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two minutes because yesterday we learned that it would be written submissions, but if it's limited to two minutes, then any of the other counsel needs one or two minutes as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was just putting the finishing touches to a written motion but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you file that, then first thing tomorrow morning, but if you say, "I can explain that in two minutes as well," then it's fine. If not, we would rather not lose further time with this witness in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I have a reputation for being economical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the Chamber is fully aware and appreciates that. Could the witness be brought into the courtroom again. Mr. Emmerson is it you who is first going to cross-examine the witness or Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Troop for Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Mr. Troop will deal with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We return into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 5th day of September, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
